subcat: The Blessing on the Poor and Woe to the Rich
text: Jesus blesses the poor for theirs is the kingdom of God, those who hunger for they will be filled, and those who weep for they will laugh. He pronounces woe when all speak well of you, for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

subcat: The Blessing on the Poor and Woe to the Rich
text: Jesus pronounces woe on the rich who have their consolation, the full who will hunger, and those who laugh now who will mourn and weep.

subcat: The Judgment of the Nations — Sheep and Goats
text: Jesus describes the Son of Man coming in glory and gathering all nations, separating them as a shepherd divides sheep from goats. The King welcomes those on his right to inherit the kingdom for feeding, clothing, and visiting him in the least of these, and sends those on the left into everlasting fire for failing to do so, the righteous going into life eternal.

subcat: The Judgment of the Nations — Sheep and Goats
text: Jesus declares that what is done for the least of these is done for him, and what is not done is withheld from him.
Jesus blesses the merciful, declaring that they will obtain mercy, and elsewhere says he desires mercy and not sacrifice.
Jesus says he has compassion on the multitude after three days with nothing to eat, and will not send them away fasting lest they faint.
Jesus asks the two blind men what they would have him do for them.
Jesus pronounces woe on Pharisees who tithe herbs but neglect judgment and the love of God, saying these should be done without neglecting the others.
Jesus sends the ten lepers to go and show themselves to the priests.
Jesus asks where the other nine are, noting that none returned to give glory to God except the one stranger, the Samaritan.
Jesus calls his first disciples to follow him, promising to make them fishers of men.
refs: Matt 4:19; Mark 1:17; Matt 19:21; John 1:43; Mark 10:18; Luke 18:19

text: Jesus warns a would-be follower that the foxes have holes and the birds of the air have nests but the Son of man has nowhere to lay his head, and tells another to follow him and let the dead bury their dead.
Jesus calls Matthew the tax collector from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
Jesus asks who is his mother and brothers, and pointing to his disciples says those who do his Father's will are his family.
Jesus calls Levi from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
Jesus calls the returning apostles to come away with him to a deserted place and rest a while.
Jesus tells Peter to launch out into the deep and let down his nets for a catch.
Jesus tells Peter not to fear, for from now on he will catch men.
Jesus calls Levi the tax collector from his tax booth with the words, follow me.
Jesus declares that no one who puts his hand to the plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.
Jesus tells the anxious Martha that she is worried and troubled about many things, but one thing is needful, and Mary has chosen that good part which will not be taken from her.
Jesus asks the first disciples what they seek and invites them to come and see where he dwells.
Jesus names Simon son of Jonah and declares that he will be called Cephas.
Jesus reminds the twelve that he has chosen them, and yet one of them is a devil.
Jesus calls his disciples to go with him into Judea again.
Jesus tells Peter that where he goes he cannot follow him now, but he will follow him afterward.

Jesus three times asks Simon son of Jonah if he loves him, charging him to feed his lambs and feed his sheep. He foretells that when Peter is old another will gird him and carry him where he would not, and calls him to follow.
Jesus declares that if anyone will come after him, let him deny himself and take up his cross and follow him.
Jesus says whoever will save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for his sake will find it. He asks what a man is profited if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul.

Jesus declares that everyone who has forsaken houses or brothers or sisters or father or mother or wife or children or lands for his name's sake will receive a hundredfold and will inherit everlasting life.
Jesus asks why his hearers call him Lord, Lord, and do not do the things he says.
Jesus rebukes James and John, saying the Son of man came not to destroy lives but to save them.
Jesus declares that whoever does not hate his own family and life, and forsake all he has, cannot be his disciple.
Jesus asks the twelve whether they also will go away.
Jesus declares that if his hearers continue in his word, then they are his disciples indeed.

Jesus teaches that a good tree brings forth good fruit and a corrupt tree evil fruit. Every tree that does not bring forth good fruit is hewn down and cast into the fire, and by their fruits they will be known.

Jesus declares that whoever loves his life will lose it, and whoever hates his life in this world keeps it for life eternal. He prays that though his soul is troubled, the Father glorify his name, for this cause he came to this hour.
Jesus declares he is the vine and his hearers the branches. Whoever abides in him bears much fruit, for without him they can do nothing.
Jesus tells his disciples he has chosen them to bear fruit that remains, and whatever they ask the Father in his name will be given.
Jesus answers the tempter that man will not live by bread alone, but by every word that proceeds from the mouth of God.
Jesus answers the tempter, declaring it is written: you will not tempt the Lord your God.
Jesus commands Satan to depart, declaring it is written: you will worship the Lord your God, and him only will you serve.
Jesus answers in Luke's account that man will not live by bread alone, but by every word of God.
Jesus rebukes Satan, declaring it is written: you will worship the Lord your God, and him only will you serve.
Jesus answers that it is said: you will not tempt the Lord your God.

Jesus blesses those persecuted for righteousness' sake, for theirs is the kingdom of heaven, and calls his hearers blessed when men revile them falsely for his sake. He charges them to rejoice, for great is their reward, as they persecuted the prophets before them.
Jesus says a prophet is not without honor, except in his own country and in his own house.
Jesus says a prophet is not without honor, except in his own country, among his own kin, and in his own house.
Jesus tells the disciples if the world hates them, it hated him first, for they are not of the world but chosen out of it.

Jesus charges the disciples to remember his word: the servant is not greater than his lord. If they have persecuted him they will also persecute them, and if they have kept his saying they will keep theirs also.

Jesus tells the disciples the world hates them because it does not know the Father. Had he not come and done such works, they had no sin; now they have seen and hated both, fulfilling the word: they hated me without a cause.
Jesus warns that they will put his disciples out of the synagogues, and the time comes when whoever kills them will think he serves God.
Jesus charges the disciples not to fear those who kill the body but cannot kill the soul, but rather to fear him who is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.
Jesus tells the disciples he has spoken these things to them so they will not stumble.

Jesus tells the disciples the world acts so because it does not know the Father, and warns them now so they will remember. He kept silent before since he was with them; now he goes to him who sent him, and sorrow fills their heart.

Jesus tells the disciples they will weep while the world rejoices, but their sorrow will turn to joy as a woman forgets her travail for joy a child is born. He will see them again, and their joy no one will take from them.
Jesus declares the hour has come when they will scatter and leave him alone, yet he is not alone because the Father is with him.
Jesus tells the disciples in him they have peace; in the world they will have tribulation, but take heart, for he has overcome the world.
Jesus answers that his grace is sufficient for him, for his strength is made perfect in weakness.

Jesus says that if anyone will come after him, let him deny himself, take up his cross, and follow him, for whoever will save his life will lose it and whoever will lose his life for his sake will find it. He declares some standing there will not taste death till they see the Son of Man coming in his kingdom.
Jesus asks what a man is profited if he gains the whole world and loses his own soul, or what a man will give in exchange for his soul.

Jesus likens this generation to children in the markets who would neither dance nor mourn, for John came neither eating nor drinking and they called him possessed, and the Son of Man comes eating and drinking and they call him a glutton.
Jesus declares that an evil and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and that none will be given but the sign of the prophet Jonah.

Jesus says of the people that they draw near to him with their mouth and honor him with their lips while their heart is far from him, and that in vain they worship him, teaching for doctrines the commandments of men.
Jesus teaches that what enters the mouth does not defile a man, but what comes from the heart defiles him: evil thoughts, murders, adulteries, thefts, false witness, and blasphemies.
Jesus declares that a wicked and adulterous generation seeks a sign, and none will be given but the sign of the prophet Jonah.
Jesus speaks to the fruitless fig tree, charging that no fruit grow on it henceforward for ever.
Jesus tells the Syrophoenician woman the children must first be filled — it is not right to give their bread to the dogs.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus tells the Pharisees that they have made the commandment of God of none effect by their tradition, calling them hypocrites of whom Esaias well prophesied.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus charges the Pharisees with setting aside the commandment of God to keep the tradition of men, such as the washing of pots and cups.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus tells the Pharisees they reject God's commandment to keep their own tradition: Moses commanded honoring father and mother, but they say a son who declares his support Corban is freed from helping them, making the word of God void.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus calls the multitude to hearken to him every one and to understand.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus explains to the disciples that whatever enters from outside cannot defile, for it goes to the belly and out, but what comes from within — that defiles the man.

subcat: Traditions of Men Versus God's Commands
text: Jesus declares that all these evil things come from within and defile the man.
Jesus asks what man among them would not lift his sheep from a pit on the sabbath, and reasons that since a man is much better than a sheep, it is lawful to do good on the sabbath.
Jesus declares that the sabbath was made for man and not man for the sabbath, and that therefore the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.
Jesus asks the Pharisees whether they have not read what David did when he was hungry, eating the showbread which was lawful only for priests.
Jesus calls the man with the withered hand to stand forth and asks whether it is lawful on the sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it.
Jesus says to the bent-over woman in the synagogue, Woman, you are loosed from yours infirmity.
Jesus calls the synagogue ruler a hypocrite, asking does not each untie his ox on the sabbath to lead him to water.
Jesus asks the lawyers and Pharisees whether it is lawful to heal on the sabbath day.
Jesus reasons that since Moses gave them circumcision and they circumcise on the sabbath so the law not be broken, they should not be angry that he has made a man whole on the sabbath.
Jesus warns that every plant which his heavenly Father has not planted will be rooted up.
Jesus concludes that these are the things which defile a man, but to eat with unwashen hands defiles not a man.
Jesus declares in the temple, my house will be called the house of prayer, but they have made it a den of thieves.

Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees sit in Moses' seat, charging his hearers to do whatever they bid but not to follow their works, for they bind heavy burdens on others' shoulders that they themselves will not lift.

Jesus says the scribes and Pharisees do their works to be seen, loving the chief seats in synagogues, greetings in markets, and the title Rabbi, and charges his disciples not to be called Rabbi, for one is their Master.

Jesus declares he sends prophets, of whom they will kill and persecute, so all righteous blood from Abel to Zacharias will come upon this generation; he laments how often he would have gathered Jerusalem's children as a hen gathers her brood, but they would not.
Jesus speaks to the unfruitful fig tree, charging that no man eat fruit of it from now on for ever.
Jesus asks in the temple, is my house not the house of prayer for all nations? You have made it a den of thieves.
Jesus answers the chief priests with a question of his own: was John's baptism from heaven or from men?
Jesus tells the chief priests, neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
Jesus tells the Pharisees they justify themselves before men, but God knows their hearts, for what men esteem highly is abomination before God.
Jesus declares in the temple that it is written, My house is the house of prayer, but they have made it a den of thieves.

Jesus tells the leaders he receives no honor from men but knows they have not the love of God in them, for they receive him not though he comes in his Father's name; he declares that Moses, in whom they trust, accuses them.

Jesus tells the religious leaders that though they are Abraham's seed, they seek to kill him because his word has no place in them, and that they do the deeds of their father the devil — a murderer from the beginning, the father of lies; because Jesus tells them the truth they do not believe him, for he that is of God hears God's words.

Jesus tells Peter that on this rock he will build his church and the gates of hell will not prevail. He gives him the keys of the kingdom of heaven — whatever he binds or looses on earth is bound or loosed in heaven.
Jesus grants the disciples authority to bind and loose: whatever they bind or loose on earth will be bound or loosed in heaven.
Jesus says where two or three gather in his name he is among them, and what two agree to ask his Father will do.
Jesus tells the disciples not to forbid the unknown man working a miracle in his name, for no one who does so can lightly speak evil of him, and whoever is not against them is for them.

Jesus declares all power in heaven and earth has been given him, charges the eleven to make disciples of all nations, baptizing in the name of the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, and promises he is with them to the end of the world.
Jesus tells the apostles they will receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon them, and be his witnesses to the ends of the earth.

subcat: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
text: Jesus charges the twelve to go to the lost sheep of Israel, taking neither gold nor extra clothing for the worker is worthy of his wages, lodging where they are received and shaking off the dust where they are not, warning them of councils and synagogues; whoever loses his life for his sake will find it, and whoever receives them receives him.

subcat: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
text: Jesus sends the twelve forth to preach that the kingdom of heaven is at hand, to heal the sick, cleanse the lepers, raise the dead, and cast out devils, charging them that as they have freely received they will freely give.

subcat: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
text: Jesus tells the twelve he sends them as sheep among wolves, and charges them therefore to be wise as serpents and harmless as doves.

subcat: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
text: Jesus tells the disciples they must go to the next towns so he may preach there also, for that is why he came forth.

subcat: Instructions for the Twelve and the Seventy
text: Jesus tells the returning seventy he beheld Satan fall as lightning from heaven, and gives them power to tread on serpents and over the enemy, charging them not to rejoice that the spirits are subject but that their names are written in heaven.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus calls out to Saul on the Damascus road, asking why he persecutes him and declaring himself to be Jesus whom Saul persecutes, and tells him it is hard to kick against the pricks and to arise and go into the city where he will be told what he must do.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus calls Ananias in a vision and sends him to lay hands on Saul of Tarsus, declaring Saul is a chosen vessel to bear his name before Gentiles, kings, and Israel, and that he will show him how much he must suffer for his name.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus tells Peter in a vision to rise, kill, and eat from the creatures let down before him, and when Peter refuses what is common or unclean, declares that what God has cleansed Peter must not call common.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus tells Paul in a vision at Corinth not to fear but to speak, for he is with him and has people in that city.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus tells Paul in a trance at the temple to make haste and depart quickly from Jerusalem, for they will not receive his testimony concerning him, and declares that he will send him far hence to the Gentiles.

subcat: Visions and Commissions to the Apostles
text: Jesus stands by Paul and bids him be of good cheer, for as he has testified in Jerusalem so must he also testify at Rome.
Jesus says that the harvest truly is plenteous but the labourers are few, and charges his disciples to pray the Lord of the harvest to send forth labourers into his harvest.

Jesus declares in the Nazareth synagogue that no prophet is accepted in his own country, recalling that in Elijah's time he was sent to a widow in Sidon and in Elisha's time only Naaman the Syrian was cleansed.
Jesus tells the crowd at Capernaum that he must preach the kingdom of God to other cities also, for to that end he was sent.

Jesus likens this generation to children who neither danced nor wept: John came neither eating nor drinking and they said he had a devil, and the Son of Man comes eating and drinking and they call him a glutton.
Jesus sends the healed Gerasene demoniac back to his own house to show how great things God has done for him.

Jesus tells the disciples his food is to do the will of him who sent him, bidding them look on the fields white for harvest, where reaper and sower rejoice together, for he sent them to reap what others have labored.
Jesus tells the disciples that they also will bear witness, because they have been with him from the beginning.
Jesus charges the disciples to preach on the housetops what they hear in the ear, and to fear not those who kill the body but him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Jesus declares that whoever confesses him before men, he will also confess before his Father in heaven, but whoever denies him before men, he will also deny before his Father in heaven.
Jesus warns the disciples that they will be brought before governors and kings for his sake as a testimony against them and the Gentiles.

Jesus warns that brother will betray brother, parents will be put to death by their children, and his disciples will be hated by all for his name's sake — but he that endures to the end will be saved.
Jesus tells the disciples that not a hair of their head will perish, and that in their patience they will possess their souls.
Jesus tells the disciples that after two days is the feast of the passover, and the Son of man is betrayed to be crucified.

Jesus defends the woman who poured ointment on him, saying she has wrought a good work upon him for his burial, and declares that wherever this gospel is preached in the whole world what she has done will be told for a memorial of her.
Jesus sends his disciples into the city to a certain man with the message that the Master's time is at hand and he will keep the passover at his house with his disciples.
Jesus declares to the Twelve at table that one of them will betray him.
Jesus says the one who dips his hand with him will betray him; the Son of Man goes as it is written, but woe to that man — it would have been good for him not to have been born.

Jesus takes the bread and cup at the supper, telling the disciples to take and eat for this is his body, and to drink for this is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and declares he will not drink of the vine again until that day in his Father's kingdom.

Jesus institutes the Lord's Supper, bidding the disciples to take and eat his body and to drink of the cup which is his blood of the new testament shed for many for the remission of sins, and pledges he will not drink of the fruit of the vine again until that day when he drinks it new with them in his Father's kingdom.

Jesus tells his disciples that all of them will be offended because of him this night — the shepherd will be smitten and the sheep scattered — but pledges that after he is risen he will go before them into Galilee.
Jesus tells Peter that this very night, before the cock crows, he will deny him three times.
Jesus tells the disciples he has longed to eat this Passover before he suffers, and will not eat it again until God's kingdom comes.
Jesus charges his disciples that the greatest among them must be as the youngest and the leader as one who serves.
Jesus asks which is greater, he who sits at table or he who serves, and declares he is among them as one who serves.

Jesus commends his disciples for continuing with him in his trials and appoints them a kingdom to eat at his table and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes; he warns Peter Satan has desired to sift him, but has prayed for him.

Jesus bids the disciples to watch with him, telling them his soul is exceeding sorrowful unto death, and prays that if possible the cup might pass yet not as he wills but the Father's; he rebukes them for not watching one hour, charging them to pray that they enter not into temptation, and at last tells them the hour is at hand.
Jesus greets Judas at the betrayal, asking, Friend, wherefore art you come?

Jesus charges Peter to put up his sword, for all who take the sword will perish; he could pray for twelve legions of angels but asks how then the scriptures should be fulfilled, and asks the arresting party why they come as against a thief.

Jesus asks the arresting party whether they have come out as against a thief with swords and staves to take him, noting that he was daily with them in the temple teaching and they took him not, but the scriptures must be fulfilled.
Jesus asks Judas whether he betrays the Son of man with a kiss.
Jesus goes forth to those who came to arrest him and asks, Whom seek you?
Jesus declares I am he to those who came to arrest him, asks again whom they seek, and tells them that since he has said he is the one, they should let his disciples go their way.
Jesus answers the high priest, you have said, and declares that from now on they will see the Son of man sitting on the right hand of power and coming in the clouds of heaven.
Jesus answers Pilate's question whether he is the King of the Jews with the words, you sayest.

Jesus tells the daughters of Jerusalem not to weep for him but for themselves and their children, for the days are coming when the barren will be called blessed and men will say to the mountains, fall on us.
Jesus tells the high priest he spoke openly in the synagogue and temple, said nothing in secret, and asks why he is questioned.
Jesus answers the officer who struck him: if he has spoken evil, bear witness of it; but if well, why is he smitten?
Jesus asks Pilate whether he says this thing of himself or whether others have told it him concerning Jesus.
Jesus tells Pilate his kingdom is not of this world; if it were, his servants would fight that he should not be delivered.
Jesus tells Pilate he came into the world to bear witness to the truth, and everyone who is of the truth hears his voice.
Jesus tells Pilate he could have no power against him unless given from above, and therefore the one who delivered him has the greater sin.
At the ninth hour Jesus cries out with a loud voice, Eli, Eli, lama sabachthani — My God, my God, why hast you forsaken me?
From the cross Jesus prays, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they do.
Jesus tells the repentant criminal crucified beside him, truly I say to you, today will you be with me in paradise.
With a loud voice Jesus cries, Father, into your hands I commend my spirit.
From the cross Jesus says to his mother, Woman, your son, and to the beloved disciple, your mother.
Jesus says from the cross, I thirst.
Jesus cries out from the cross, It is finished.
Jesus joins the two disciples on the Emmaus road and asks what they are discussing as they walk so sadly.
Jesus walks with the Emmaus disciples and asks what things, drawing out their account of Jesus of Nazareth.
Jesus calls the two disciples fools and slow of heart to believe the prophets, asking whether the Christ had to suffer to enter his glory.
Jesus appears among the gathered disciples on the resurrection evening and greets them, saying peace to you.

Jesus asks why they are troubled and why doubts arise in their hearts. He bids them handle his hands and feet, for a spirit has no flesh and bones. He reminds them that Moses, the prophets, and the psalms all speak of him.
Jesus asks the disciples whether they have any food there.

Jesus tells the disciples it is written that the Christ would suffer and rise the third day, that repentance and forgiveness of sins would be preached in his name to all nations beginning at Jerusalem, and that they are witnesses of these things.

Jesus asks Mary why she weeps and calls her by name, sending her to tell his brethren he ascends to his Father. He gives the disciples peace, sends them as he was sent with the Holy Spirit, and grants authority to remit or retain sins.
From the shore Jesus asks if they have food and tells them to cast the net on the right side and they will find.
Jesus instructs the disciples to bring of the fish they have just caught.
Jesus invites the disciples to come and dine.
Jesus returns eight days later with Thomas present and greets the disciples, saying peace to you.

Jesus tells Thomas to reach his finger and see his hands, and to thrust his hand into his side, charging him not to be faithless but believing. He declares blessed are those who have not seen and yet believed.
Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, declaring that there will not be left one stone upon another that will not be thrown down.
Jesus warns his disciples to take heed that no one deceive them, for many will come in his name claiming to be Christ; iniquity will abound and the love of many will grow cold.

Jesus tells his disciples they will hear of wars and rumors of wars but not be troubled, for nation will rise against nation and there will be famines and earthquakes — these are the beginning of sorrows.
Jesus declares that this gospel of the kingdom will be preached in all the world for a witness, and then the end will come.

Jesus warns that when his hearers see the abomination of desolation standing in the holy place, those in Judea must flee to the mountains without turning back, for then will be great tribulation such as has not been since the beginning of the world; for the elect's sake those days will be shortened.
Jesus warns that false christs and false prophets will arise and show great signs, so that, if possible, even the elect will be deceived.

Jesus says after that tribulation the sun will be darkened and the stars will fall; then the sign of the Son of Man will appear, and the tribes of the earth will mourn at his coming in the clouds with power and great glory.
Jesus foretells the destruction of the temple, declaring that not one stone will be left upon another that will not be thrown down.

Jesus weeps over Jerusalem, lamenting that she did not know the things that belong to her peace; the days will come when her enemies will lay her with the ground and not leave one stone upon another, because she knew not her visitation.
Jesus foretells that the days will come when not one stone of the temple will be left upon another.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus declares that his disciples will be hated of all men for his name's sake, but he that endures to the end will be saved.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus promises his followers that when the Son of Man sits on his throne of glory, they will sit on twelve thrones judging Israel's tribes.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus declares the Son of Man's coming will be like lightning from east to west, and as in Noah's days they ate and married till the flood came, so will his coming be; he says heaven and earth will pass away but his words will not, and that of that day no one knows — not the angels, but the Father only.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus declares that the sign of the Son of Man will appear and the tribes of the earth will mourn at his coming in the clouds with power, and he will send his angels with a trumpet to gather his elect from the four winds.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus says that two will be in the field, the one taken and the other left, and two women will be grinding at the mill, the one taken and the other left.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus warns his disciples they will long for the days of the Son of Man unseen, and not to chase rumors of his coming.

subcat: The Return of the Son of Man
text: Jesus declares from the throne that he makes all things new, promising the water of life to the thirsty and warning the unfaithful of the lake of fire.
Jesus charges his hearers to watch, for they know not what hour their Lord does come.
Jesus interrupts the bowl-judgment vision to declare he comes as a thief, and blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments.

Jesus declares I come quickly — blessed is he that keeps the sayings of the prophecy of this book — and that his reward is with him to give every man according as his work will be, affirming surely I come quickly.

subcat: The Fig Tree and the Unknown Hour
text: Jesus declares that heaven and earth will pass away but his words will not pass away, says that of that day and hour knows no man — not the angels of heaven, but the Father only — and likens his coming to a thief whose hour the householder does not know, charging his hearers therefore to be ready.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus declares it will be more tolerable for Sodom and Gomorrah at the judgment than for cities that reject his messengers, and says the hour comes when all in the graves will hear his voice and come forth to life or damnation.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus says men will give account for every idle word, and his word will judge those who reject him on the last day.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus declares that Nineveh and the queen of the South will condemn this generation, for one greater than Jonah and Solomon is here.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus says the Son of Man will come in the glory of his Father with his angels and reward every man according to his works, for the Father has committed all judgment to the Son.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus says he goes his way and his hearers will seek him and die in their sins, for where he goes they cannot come.

subcat: The Certainty and Scope of Judgment
text: Jesus tells the crowd the voice came for their sakes; now is the judgment of this world, and its prince will be cast out.
Jesus warns that anger with a brother brings danger of judgment, calling him Raca brings the council, and saying You fool brings hell fire.
Jesus charges that if eye or hand offends, cut it off — better to lose one member than have the whole body cast into hell.
Jesus declares that the children of the kingdom will be cast out into outer darkness, where there will be weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Jesus tells his disciples to fear not the killers of the body but him who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
Jesus declares that at the end of the age angels will cast the wicked into the furnace of fire, with wailing and gnashing of teeth.

Jesus says if a hand or foot offends, cut it off — better to enter life maimed than with two hands or two feet to be cast into everlasting fire, into hell, where the worm does not die and the fire is not quenched.
Jesus tells how the king binds the man hand and foot and casts him into outer darkness, with weeping and gnashing of teeth.
Jesus cries out to the scribes and Pharisees as serpents and a brood of vipers, asking how they will escape the damnation of hell.
Jesus declares those on his left will go into everlasting fire prepared for the devil — to everlasting punishment, the righteous to life eternal.
Jesus declares that many will come from the east and west and will sit down with Abraham and Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom of heaven.

Jesus declares the hour is coming when the dead will hear the voice of the Son of God and live, says he is the resurrection and the life, and promises to raise up at the last day all the Father has given him.

subcat: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
text: Jesus declares that he is Alpha and Omega, the beginning and the ending, the Lord who is and was and is to come, the Almighty.

subcat: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
text: Jesus, the first and the last, charges John to write what he sees and send it to the seven churches in Asia.

subcat: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
text: Jesus tells John not to fear, for he is the first and the last, alive forevermore, holding the keys of hell and death.

subcat: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
text: Jesus charges John to write what is and what will be — the stars are the church angels and the candlesticks are the churches.

subcat: Introduction to the Seven Churches — The Vision of Christ
text: Jesus closes each of the seven letters with the same summons, charging him that has an ear to hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

subcat: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
text: Jesus addresses the angel of the church of Ephesus as the one who holds the seven stars and walks among the seven golden candlesticks.

subcat: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
text: Jesus commends Ephesus for their works and patience and testing of false apostles, but holds against them that they have left their first love, charging them to remember from where they have fallen, repent, and do the first works, or he will remove their candlestick.

subcat: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
text: Jesus commends Ephesus that they hate the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which he also hates.

subcat: Ephesus — The Church That Left Its First Love
text: Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give to eat of the tree of life in the paradise of God.
Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Smyrna as the first and the last, who was dead and is alive.
Jesus tells Smyrna not to fear what they will suffer but to be faithful unto death, and he will give them a crown of life.
Jesus charges Smyrna to be faithful unto death for the crown of life; he who overcomes will not be hurt of the second death.
Jesus addresses the angel of the church in Pergamos as the one who has the sharp sword with two edges.

Jesus commends Pergamos for holding fast his name even where Satan dwells, but holds against them that some hold the doctrines of Balaam and the Nicolaitans, charging them to repent or he will fight against them with the sword of his mouth.
Jesus promises that to him who overcomes he will give the hidden manna and a white stone with a new name written on it.

subcat: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
text: Jesus addresses Thyatira as the Son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire and whose feet are like fine brass.

subcat: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
text: Jesus commends Thyatira's works but holds against them that they suffer Jezebel, who seduces his servants to fornication and idolatry, and declares he will cast her into a bed and her children into death, that all may know he searches hearts.

subcat: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
text: Jesus tells the rest in Thyatira who have not held this doctrine that he will put on them no other burden.

subcat: Thyatira — The Church Tolerating False Teaching
text: Jesus charges Thyatira to hold fast what they have until he comes, and promises that to him who overcomes he will give power over the nations and the morning star.

Jesus tells Sardis that they have a name that they live but are dead, charging them to be watchful, strengthen what remains, and repent, or he will come on them as a thief at an hour they do not know.
Jesus says a few in Sardis have not defiled their garments, and they will walk with him in white, for they are worthy.
Jesus promises he who overcomes will wear white, with his name kept in the book of life and confessed before the Father.
Jesus addresses Philadelphia as the holy and true one with the key of David — opens what none can shut, shuts what none can open.

Jesus tells Philadelphia he has set before them an open door no one can shut, for they have a little strength and have kept his word, and promises to keep them from the hour of trial that comes upon all the world.
Jesus comes quickly and charges Philadelphia to hold fast their crown, and promises him who overcomes a pillar in the temple of his God.
Jesus addresses the angel of the church of the Laodiceans as the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God.

Jesus rebukes Laodicea for being lukewarm and declares he will spit them out, telling them that though they say they are rich they are wretched and naked, counseling them to buy gold, white raiment, and eyesalve, and charging them to be zealous and repent.
Jesus stands at the door and knocks; if any opens he will come in. He who overcomes will sit with him on his throne.
